text:
jules: Quick thread 14: after the mini-window fastpath landing, were getting unexpected medium-tail regressions on mixed traffic. Need design tradeoff brainstorm.

ravi: Seen similar locally. p95 ok, p99 for 200-600 token requests jumps. Is KV thrash the root cause?

jules: Telemetry shows two things: 1) medium reqs repeatedly miss KV and cause cache churn, 2) many mediums get appended to later coalesce rounds (queueing) because short requests keep closing windows.

anya: Could be coalesce-depth bias. We currently prioritize closing a window after 3ms or N requests, whichever first. Short spikes bias the timing.

ravi: Two families of fixes: a) keep single continuous batcher but add length-aware headroom/reservations, b) split execution into lanes (micro-lane for medium+) and route.

jules: Single-path advantage = fewer context switches and simpler telemetry paths. Lane split advantage = explicit isolation. Both have cost.

tao: Note: routing to lane requires token accounting and KV affinity considerations. If you move a request off the main pool, you might lose prefix cache locality benefits.

anya: Proposal sketch (hybrid): keep continuous batcher, add a cheap pre-admit reservation for anything with estimated_tokens >= 150 when current_coalesce_rounds < MIN_ROUNDS. If reservation granted, we mark a soft slot and avoid early coalescing on that tenant until slot used.

ravi: Add per-tenant sliding budget to prevent a noisy tenant from hogging these soft slots. If budget exceeded, route to lane B (micro-lane) which has isolated batching but potentially higher p50.

jules: Pseudocode (very rough):
```
if est_tokens >= 150 and coalesce_rounds < 2 and tenant.soft_budget > est_tokens+headroom:
  tenant.soft_budget -= est_tokens+headroom
  mark_reserved_slot(tenant)
  prevent_early_drain(tenant)
else:
  normal_opportunistic_join()
```

tao: Important: estimate errors. We should cap headroom and add a reclaim path: if reservation not consumed within X ms, release slot. Also track `reservation_miss_rate`.

anya: Metrics to add for the canary: `soft_reserved_slots`, `reservation_releases`, `kv_cache_evictions_by_slot`, `micro_lane_routing_rate`, `p99_by_length_class`.

ravi: Rollout plan: small canary (5 tenants) -> collect 72h metrics -> expand to 25 tenants. Gate on kv_evictions down and medium p99 down.

jules: Operational knobs: disable by setting medium_threshold=9999 or turn off per-tenant budgets. Make rollback a single flag flip.

tao: Edge case: bursts of shorts could still occupy GPU and delay consumption of reserved slots. Mitigation: prioritization inside coalesce: if reserved slot present, try to ensure that reserved request is included before closing. That requires per-slot visibility in coalesce decision.

anya: That touches interface boundary: coalescer currently lacks awareness of reservation metadata. We'll add a tiny API: `reserve_hint(tenant, tokens)` that coalescer checks during finalize. Minimal surface.

ravi: Also ensure tracing and spans include `reservation_id` so we can correlate tail spikes to reservation behavior.

jules: Action items: 1) rama/anya to prototype pre-admit + per-tenant soft budget in bench harness, 2) tao to add metrics and tracing tags, 3) ops to prepare canary rollout doc with kill-switch.

ops-bot: Canary checklist created: batcher/pre-admit-reservation -> canary-gpu-pool-2 (owner: ops).

jules: I'll land a tiny follow-up note in the RFC thread describing the escape hatch and interface (`reserve_hint`) plus the budget model. Keep it short.

ravi: One more thought 14 if reservation misses are frequent (estimation wrong), fallback path should penalize estimation source and drop headroom. We need an online calibration metric to adjust default headroom per tenant class.

anya: Good call. Let's keep the initial headroom conservative (32 tokens) and tune from canary.

jules: Ok team. We'll reconvene after 72h of canary metrics. Thanks. :rocket:
